hooks.description: Inject Propel session state on start and resume: Codex state, mode and the automatic mode-selection policy, active investigations, project profile, empty-repo flag, registry entries
Inject Propel's core principles (core/CORE.md) — its own hook entry because Claude Code truncates a single hook's output above ~10,000 characters
Inject the dual-model Codex policy (core/CODEX.md) — its own hook entry to stay under the per-hook output cap
Inject part 1 of the using-propel skill (routing and gates), split across hook entries to stay under the per-hook output cap
Inject part 2 of the using-propel skill (routing and gates), split across hook entries to stay under the per-hook output cap
Inject part 3 of the using-propel skill (routing and gates), split across hook entries to stay under the per-hook output cap
Inject part 4 of the using-propel skill (routing and gates), split across hook entries to stay under the per-hook output cap
Inject prior experiments and architecture designs so new proposals don't duplicate past work
Re-state the active mode, the Codex state, and the routing rules every turn so automatic dispatch doesn't decay as context fills
After every source edit, state which auditors are required before Gate 3 — makes auditor dispatch deterministic instead of remembered
